Which one to power up? Compare IVs of the same Pokémon

Input

1Which Pokémon?

Compare as which form?

2Where will you use it?

3How far will you power it up?

For GO Battle League, it assumes you power up to the highest level that fits under the CP cap.

4Enter the Pokémon you have

Attack, Defense and HP are 0–15. Add the CP too and it works out the current level — wild, raid or trade — to give the exact Stardust to the target level. Left blank, level 20 is assumed.

Results

Power up this one
Within 1% · about the same

How it picks

  • Since it is the same Pokémon, moves are assumed to be the same; only Attack, Defense and HP at the target level are compared.
  • Type a type (e.g. Dragon) or a move name (e.g. Meteor Mash) in the name box to get a list of matching Pokémon. Typing a name also shows its evolution family.
  • Pick a Pokémon before evolution and you can compare it as its evolved form. IVs stay the same when it evolves, so use this to decide which Dratini to raise into Dragonite. Candy for evolving is not included in the Stardust column.
  • In big-group raids, finishing fast matters, so Attack is weighted heavily. For small groups and solo, staying power counts too.
  • Shadow Pokémon are calculated as dealing 1.2× damage and taking 1.2× damage.
  • If the difference is within 1%, it picks the one that needs less Stardust (Lucky, or already powered up).
  • Cases where the damage per hit against a specific boss comes out the same (breakpoints) are not reflected yet.
  • GO Battle League compares Attack × Defense × HP (stat product) at the highest level under the CP cap. The rank is its place among all 4,096 IV combinations of the same Pokémon.
  • Who moves first when Attack ties (CMP) and breakpoints against specific opponents are not reflected.
  • A Pokémon whose current CP is already over the league cap cannot go down in level, so it cannot be used in that league.
